name: room
text: Room opened — goal: visual: Mine AI website/product DESIGNS (the look), taste-learn from Eitan's picks.

name: Easel
text: To achieve our goal of mining AI website/product designs, I propose we start by curating a collection of Eitan's picks, as they will serve as a foundation for our design inspiration. This decision will allow us to establish a consistent aesthetic and make informed choices about the visual elements that will represent our brand. By focusing on Eitan's picks first, we're accepting the trade-off of potentially limiting our initial scope, but this will enable us to create a cohesive design language from the outset. This approach will ultimately save us time and effort in the long run by ensuring our design decisions are intentional and aligned with our desired visual identity.

name: Squint
text: Squint: Starting with Eitan’s picks as the *only* foundation risks locking us into one aesthetic before we’ve even explored what makes AI products *work*—not just look. A better alternative is to first audit live AI sites (e.g., Perplexity, Midjourney) to extract patterns in layout, hierarchy, and interaction, then layer Eitan’s taste on top. Settle it by testing both approaches with a quick prototype: if Eitan’s picks lead to a clearer visual language, we adopt them; if not, we pivot to the audit.
